intended_object: The closed form of the third partial derivative ∂_m∂_j∂_l(1/|x|) of the inverse Euclidean radius on ℝ³ \ {0}. This comes from the docstring and from the lemma at line 335, which identifies it with the spatial third derivative of the radial inverse. It is used to build the third derivative of the Newtonian kernel −1/(4π|x|).
explanation:
Direct computation, with r = |x| and δ the Kronecker delta:
- ∂_j(1/r) = −x_j/r³.
- ∂_l∂_j(1/r) = −δ_{jl}/r³ + 3x_jx_l/r⁵.
- ∂_m∂_l∂_j(1/r) = 3(δ_{jl}x_m + δ_{jm}x_l + δ_{lm}x_j)/r⁵ − 15x_jx_lx_m/r⁷.

This is exactly what the body says. The library also proves (line 335) that it equals the iterated spatial derivative of the radial inverse when x ≠ 0.

At x = 0 the formula evaluates to 0, because Lean takes 0⁻¹ = 0. This is a harmless junk value: the derivative is not defined there.

The definition is tied to ℝ³ (`Fin 3`), the setting of the Newtonian kernel 1/(4π|x|) used for the Navier–Stokes analysis in this library. In dimension d the Newtonian kernel is a different power, |x|^{2−d}, so restricting to d = 3 is part of the content, not an arbitrary narrowing. Mathlib has no closed form for derivatives of 1/|x|.
